name: Grounded chat turn handler
description: Turns a chat message about someone's own quests into a reply built from what their account holds, or into the exact change they asked for.
purpose: Answer a person's chat message from the facts held in their own account, and carry out exactly the changes the message asks for.
approach: Ground each reply in reads of the person's account, and make only the writes the request asks for.
out_of_scope: Bulk or scheduled work that needs no conversational reply.
milestones: 1. Share of dev chat cases passed by the cheapest tier (haiku): 100%, at a cost per passing turn of a few cents. Set by Joshua on 2026-10-19; no dollar ceiling per turn is set.
knowledge: Recorded misses repeat: asking which quest or for data the quest already holds, proposing instead of writing when the request was unambiguous, stating an unsupported fact, and ending a multi-step request with a queued task and no report of what is unfinished. A turn can take many model calls, so cost per passing turn matters. A rubric judged by a model is not yet calibrated against human verdicts, and a small sample cannot rank two implementations.
measures_of_success: On a rich, realistic disposable account, hard deterministic checks pass first (reply text, routing, side effects, tools called) and a judge finds every rubric item met. Repeated runs of the same case agree. Standing conditions: Minimise side effects that were not requested, unsupported claims, needless questions about data the account already holds, and model calls per passing turn.
parameters: The model tier or pinned model for the chat, the model-call budget for an evaluation run, and the quest the turn is scoped to.
inputs: The user message, the conversation so far, the account's quests and data reachable through read tools, and the context the host supplies.
outputs: The reply text, the routing taken (inline or delegated), the tools called, and any queued or delegated work with its status.
effects: Reads account data, may write quest data the user asked for, may queue a deep run, and spends model tokens.
usage_notes: Use the evaluation arm only against a disposable world, never real data. Run the offline validity arm first to confirm the checks can tell a good reply from none, then the live arm on a small stratified sample.

name: Mode-aware progress surfacing
description: Decides what a person sees of a run by how they follow it: every event while they watch live, only the milestones once the run moves to the background, and nothing it does can break the run itself.
purpose: Lets a person follow a run at the level they want, every step while they watch and only milestones once they step away.
approach: Chooses which events of a run reach a person, according to whether they are watching live or in the background.
out_of_scope: Deciding which events a run produces, since this solution only chooses which of them are shown.
milestones: 1. Live mode shows every event in order, background mode shows only results, decisions, milestones, context, tokens and done, and a broken stream never stops a run: all 14 offline cases pass. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: Messaging policy lives in one place, the sinks, so the orchestrator only emits. Chatter such as planning and reading is dropped in the background so users are not spammed. A detach hands a live run to the background sink. This scores the sinks, not what the orchestrator emits.
measures_of_success: Each mode surfaces exactly its stated set, order is preserved, a mid-run detach switches policy cleanly, and a failing stream or callback is swallowed. Standing conditions: Ensure live mode shows every event in order and background mode shows only result, decision, milestone, context, tokens and done. Never let a broken stream or callback stop the run.
parameters: The mode, the forward function for the live stream, and the per-event callbacks for the background sink.
inputs: A progress event with a type and text, and the current mode.
outputs: None returned; surfaced events reach the consumer's stream or callbacks.
effects: Calls consumer callbacks or pushes to a stream; swallows their failures.
usage_notes: Pick the sink by mode, fan out when a live run may detach, and keep sinks free of side effects beyond forwarding.

name: Learned-operation fast path
description: Repeats a previously successful tool operation without a context search, so a repeat request skips the planning step and its model calls.
purpose: Speeds up a quest's repeated operations by recognising a request that worked before and replaying the known steps.
approach: Recognises a repeated request by its match to a recorded successful operation and replays it, filling only the arguments.
out_of_scope: Lookalike writes that only resemble a recorded operation, and plain conversation.
milestones: 1. Recipe replay and the planner-only path reach the same pass rate on repeat requests when both run live through the claude CLI, with recipe replay making fewer model calls and its hit rate recorded.
knowledge: A lookalike request must never trigger a write, so replay carries a guard for mutating operations and a minimum match score. The offline arm uses a rule model written with the cases in view, so it proves the engine, not a real model's judgment. Recipes are learned only from successes.
measures_of_success: Right tool and arguments on a repeat, no tool on a near miss or on chat, a large share of repeats served from recipes, and fewer model calls than the planner-only path at the same pass rate.
parameters: The recipe store path (or none for memory only), the minimum match score, scope tags for learning and matching, and the planner model tier.
inputs: A user request and the registry of available tools.
outputs: The reply text and exit reason of the run, with the tool executed and its arguments when a recipe fired.
effects: Learns a new recipe after a successful operation and rewrites the recipe file atomically under a lock; may execute a tool.
usage_notes: Enable by configuring a recipe store on the orchestrator; compare against a planner-only run on the same tasks before trusting it, and keep mutating operations behind the guard.

name: Budgeted prompt assembler
description: Derives the size limit of every prompt from the cheapest model's window and the cost per call, so each prompt is sized against a stated budget rather than by guesswork.
purpose: Compose each prompt from its parts within a size budget and without repeated blocks, so every call stays inside the model window and its cost limit.
approach: Build each prompt from its parts within a budget derived from the model window and cost per call, and include each block only once.
out_of_scope: Judging whether the content is the right content for a prompt, and joining parts with no size limit.
milestones: 1. Assembly points under their budget on all 11 size fixtures, with zero duplicated blocks. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: An incident showed prompts growing past what the cheapest tier tolerates, so budgets are derived from the cheapest tier's window, a stated share and the cost per call. The shares and cost caps are policy to be confirmed by a human, and the fixtures are generated filler at incident sizes, not real content.
measures_of_success: Every assembly point stays under budget on all fixtures with reported headroom, and no block appears twice. Standing conditions: Keep the size at each assembly point under its budget, keep duplicated blocks at zero, and leave headroom under healthy, incident and production-sized inputs.
parameters: Per assembly point budgets from the budget inputs file, the autopilot brief token budget, and the fitting policy for goal prompts.
inputs: The planner message, transcript, context view and gathered results; the autopilot batch parts; a context-update bundle; and a goal, brief and preamble for a deep prompt.
outputs: The assembled prompt string for each assembly point.
effects: None beyond the prompt; fitting may drop or shorten low-priority parts to stay inside the budget.
usage_notes: Route any new prompt through the shared fitting module and add its assembly point and fixtures to the evaluation so its budget is checked.

name: Core ML tasks
description: Puts the Quest classification and recommendation tasks under one measured choice, so each method is picked by held-out accuracy and cost rather than by habit.
purpose: Help every Quest feature that classifies a quest or input, or recommends a next goal, step or quest, use the most accurate method its measurements support.
approach: Choose the classification or recommendation method for each Quest task by its measured accuracy on held-out cases, with cost as the tie-break.
out_of_scope: Routing a single chat message to an answer, a tool or a deep run.
milestones: 1. Accuracy on held-out labelled cases is recorded for shared-quest-ranker and hybrid-candidate-ranker, then for the area-of-life and recommendation alternatives.
knowledge: Requested by Joshua on 2026-10-19: quest classification and recommendation are the main ML tasks used across Quest and have had alternative implementations. Located in code on 2026-10-19: which-quest classification in quest-backend quest_selection.py (the shared ranker) and quest_candidates.py (the chat's hybrid ranker); area-of-life classification in categories/search.py and planets_service.py; quest-to-intent placement and intent recommendation in intents/suggest.py; next-period goal placement in period_review_ai.py; message routing in evaluation/components/classification.
measures_of_success: Each task has a labelled case set with a held-out share, and every alternative has a recorded result on it; the selected alternative is the best by accuracy with cost as tie-break.
parameters: The task (classify or recommend), the implementation, and the model tier where one is used.
inputs: The quest, input text or user data to classify, or the person's quests, goals and history to recommend from.
outputs: A class or a ranked list with a score for each, and the cost of producing it.
effects: May spend model tokens; reads user data; writes nothing.
usage_notes: Define a case set per task first, then register each existing alternative as an implementation of this solution.

name: How-I-got-this explanation
description: Decides the prose that tells a person how an answer was reached, with a model call that is kept only while its measured value outweighs its cost and time.
purpose: Gives a person the prose that tells a person how an answer was reached at a cost and delay that its metric accepts.
approach: A prompt declared as a prompt spec makes one model call to write, from the turn's trace, how the answer was reached.
out_of_scope: Choosing the model tier (choose-a-model-tier) and the surrounding turn or run.
milestones: 1. Its metric has a case set and a recorded result for the current arm and the no-model floor. 2. The model call stays only while it beats the floor on the metric.
knowledge: Proposed 2026-10-28 so that this prompt has a solution and a metric that justify its cost, time and value; not built, so the metric is unmeasured and the current call is a direction, not a measured win.
measures_of_success: The metric is read from the cases without invented readings. Standing conditions: Never invent a reading. Add no time before a chat reply.
parameters: The model tier and any cap the module states.
inputs: The text or events the call is given.
outputs: The text or verdict the call returns.
effects: One model call; no write beyond the text it returns.
usage_notes: Selected today: model_explanation. The floor is a proposed arm with no model call. Decision teamdec_96793b0729b9 (see docs/explanation/answer-explanation.md).

name: Whole-path answer check
description: Measures whether QAR answers well overall: one message goes through the whole path (route, context, plan, act, answer) and is judged by what changed in the world and what the reply says.
purpose: Tell, with one cheap run, whether a person's message is handled right end to end across the kinds of request QAR serves, so that a gap in any part of the path shows as a failed turn and is fixed before a part is discarded.
approach: A small labelled set of messages, each sent into a placeholder account behind the real tool catalogue and the real orchestrator; the score reads the writes, the route, the web queries and the reply, never a model judge.
out_of_scope: Judging prose quality, long conversations, and the model tier choice (choose-a-model-tier); the dev-account chat metric (answer-a-turn) and the part metrics stay as they are.
milestones: 1. The set has a recorded run for the current arm and the no-model floor on the current commit. 2. A failed turn is read and its defect fixed or its case corrected before the run is repeated.
knowledge: Proposed 2026-10-29 so that the whole path has one measure; the label set is rewritten from chat_quality, quest_ops and assist_a_terminal_session cases and is small, so it is a smoke measure, not a ranking.
measures_of_success: Turns are scored from the world afterwards. Standing conditions: Never write what was not asked. Never answer an absent fact as present.
parameters: The planner tier of the live arm and the model-call budget of a run.
inputs: One message, the pinned quest or none, and the placeholder account.
outputs: The reply, the writes that landed, the web queries made and the route taken.
effects: Model calls on the live arm through the Claude Code subscription; no write beyond the in-memory placeholder account.
usage_notes: Run the scripted arm and the floor first (free), then the live arm on a few cases, then more, then the set, under the lock for heavy jobs.

name: Show the AI's work and next steps
description: Decides what a person sees of the work the AI did for their reply, beside the reply: nothing, a plain list of every step, or the Trail (a live line, one summary line and expandable groups), the same for the person who asked and for the other people in a group or team chat, live and from history. Its presentation side is in quest-frontend (solution show-the-ais-work there); this record holds the arms, the cases and the measurement.
purpose: Lets a person trust an answer because they can see it rests on real work done for their question, without being shown anything that does not earn its place.
approach: The run emits typed work_trace events from structural results (core/work_trace.py, contract in the hub); the app shows them. Three arms are measured on the same turns by one metric: truthfulness as a gate, the share of shown elements that earn their place, and parity between viewers.
out_of_scope: What the run emits is core/work_trace.py (checked by work_trace_check). Which progress events reach a person by mode is show-progress. Interim replies and asks in chat are another design and are not recorded here until built and measured.
milestones: 1. The Trail is built and mounted on the solo, shared-list and team chat surfaces. 2. All three arms have a recorded offline row and a recorded row on real turns. 3. A reviewed set of real-turn screenshots (sender and other participant, 390px and 1280px, light and dark, live and settled).
knowledge: docs/explanation/live-work-trace.md (the contract, the Trail, the review rules); the real turns captured by evaluation/components/work_trace_experience/live_turns.py; the 2026-11-01 first real runs found: a search that opened no page showed nothing, a live line read 'Reading 0 of N sites' when nothing had been opened, sites a search only listed were shown as read, one paper under two DOIs was counted twice and three searches' totals were added into one papers-found figure far above the papers shown.
measures_of_success: metric-work-trace-experience: a turn is passed when what is shown is true, the same for every viewer, present when there was work to show, and every shown element earns its place. Standing conditions: Never show a count above what the run did. Never show another person's record titles in a shared thread. Show nothing for a turn without work.
parameters: Which arm the app runs (the Trail today); QUEST_AI_WORK_TRACE=off in the backend switches the trace off.
inputs: The turn's work_trace events in arrival order, or the saved list of finished steps, and whether the thread is shared.
outputs: The elements a viewer is shown: a live line, a summary line and expandable groups, or a flat list, or nothing.
effects: None beyond display; the saved reply carries the finished steps.
usage_notes: Selected today: trail. The arms' rules live in quest-frontend (src/utils/workTrace.ts, src/components/chat/ai/WorkTrace.tsx); evaluation/components/work_trace_experience runs them through scripts/run-worktrace-view.js there, so a sibling quest-frontend checkout (or QUEST_FRONTEND_DIR) is needed to measure.

name: Reply in steps when the goal is not met yet
description: Decides, from the verifier's verdict and the run's own record, whether an attempt that did not meet the goal sends an interim message now (what is done so far and why more is coming), at most a few per turn, never when the blocker is a person, a fault or nothing new. Off by default (OrchestratorConfig.interim_replies); both the policy and its switch are in core/interim_policy.py. It also decides the one ask a block that only a person can lift needs: a decision request to the right person, once per gap, instead of text that only looks like a question.
purpose: Lets a person see progress and the reason for more work during a long turn without being spammed.
approach: A pure decision over structural inputs (enum verdict, whether the loop runs again, an open ask, receipts and coverage, a clock and two counters); nothing reads the wording of model output.
out_of_scope: Whether and how the app groups and collapses the messages (quest-frontend), and the work trace (show-the-ais-work).
milestones: 1. The offline cases pass for the real policy and fail for the spam baseline. 2. One real turn on haiku through the claude CLI is hand read with the switch on.
measures_of_success: metric-interim-reply-truthful-and-useful. Standing conditions: Never send an interim unless another attempt follows. Never repeat a message with nothing new in it. Never read the wording of model output to decide.
inputs: The attempt's verdict, receipts, coverage and the turn's ledger.
outputs: Send or skip with a reason, and the interim event payload.
effects: None; the caller emits the event.
usage_notes: Selected today: gated (code exists; the switch is off, so the live behaviour is the incumbent until it is turned on). The incumbent today and the spam baseline are measurement arms only.
